Crop rotation with rice for at least three years.
Avoid new cultivations on lands that have a history of this disease.
Random indexing of suckers for the freeness of the pathogen.
Monitoring: Regular visits to the farm for identification of the disease
Observe for characteristic symptoms such as yellowing and lodging of outer mature leaves or splitting of the base of the pseudo-stem
Any suspected plants that are observed should be cut open for the examination of internal symptoms.
At plantations in risky areas, periodically inspect healthy suckers for internal initial browning symptoms in the rhizome.
Management options should be made immediately after first symptoms observed.
Direct Control: Immediately after detection of the disease, remove and destroy by burning infected plants along with the rhizome, roots and infected soil.

Add lime or wood ash to the infected soil.
Avoid surface irrigation through the infected areas.
Isolate the infected spots by constructing drains and bunds.
